summary: WebSocket streaming stalls mid-generation after client cellular handoff (4G->5G)
description:
Issue summary: WebSocket-based streaming responses for a long-form chat request intermittently stall and stop sending tokens after clients switch network connectivity (observed during 4G->5G handoff). Customer reports that the client-side socket remains open but no additional chunks arrive for ~20-90s, after which the connection either recovers or the server closes the socket with 502.

Impact: Multiple paying customers using LinguaChat's dedicated Redwood pool see degraded UX for long chats (5–20 minute responses). Symptoms started around 2026-03-12 22:10 UTC and correlate with increased tail latencies and a spike in worker preemptions. Affects ~3% of long-stream sessions for this customer during the incident window.

Environment: Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated GPU pool), production, us-east-1. Traffic routed through our edge websocket-proxy, then to per-tenant dedicated serving-runtime instances.

Observed behavior: Streaming halts mid-token sequence after client experiences cellular handoff. Server traces show in-flight request marked as "active" but no socket writes for 20–90s. Upstream worker remains healthy (CPU/GPU not saturated) and KV cache appears consistent. Edge logs show TLS session renegotiate events from the client IP at the time of stall.

Expected behavior: Streaming continues uninterrupted or fails-fast with a clear error and model fallback; tokens should not silently stop with socket left open.

Initial customer impact notes: LinguaChat reports multiple user sessions where the chat response stops for ~30s then resumes with a burst of tokens or the client shows an indefinite loading spinner. Customer escalated since it affects demo flows and user retention.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a mobile client connected to a 4G network and start a long-form chat request that triggers a multi-minute generation.
2) While the model is generating, trigger a cellular network handoff (4G -> 5G) or switch between mobile carriers (can be emulated via network conditioning tools).
3) Observe websocket traffic: client reports connection stays ESTABLISHED, but token frames cease for 20–90s (server-side), then either resume or the connection returns 502/connection-reset.
4) Capture server trace IDs and edge-proxy logs around the time of the handoff for analysis.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC - Initial triage (Aisha): Correlated customer reports with a small spike in websocket idle-write timeouts and with an increase in TLS renegotiation events from mobile IP ranges.

2026-03-13 05:20 UTC - SRE (Diego): Pulled edge-proxy traces for affected trace IDs; observed that the socket remained open and proxy did not send FIN. No obvious OOM or worker OOM events on serving runtime.

2026-03-13 07:45 UTC - Hypothesis: Cellular handoff triggers TCP-level transient retransmits and causes the edge-proxy to enter a backoff path that suppresses writes to the client for safety, but the serving runtime continues generating tokens into outgoing buffers, leading to buffer pressure and eventual socket close by upstream (502) or silent stall.

2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Reproduced in staging: Simulated handoff with network emulator; saw keepalive packets reach proxy but a burst of retransmissions. When kernel TCP retransmit count exceeded threshold, proxy returned 0 bytes to worker and stalled for ~30s.

2026-03-13 11:00 UTC - Correlated with recent edge-proxy change: rolling deploy of proxy v2.17 introduced conservative write-coalescing when retransmit_count > 3 (PR 4123), which may amplify stalls for long-lived streaming sockets.
comments: Support (Aisha Kumar) 2026-03-13: Customer reports 8 sessions affected in the last 24h; provided sample trace IDs and HAR of websocket session. Asked for priority handling due to demo impact.
SRE (Diego Ramirez) 2026-03-13: Replicated stall in staging using network emulation. Opening follow-up with edge team to revert/coarsen new write-coalescing threshold as a hotfix.
Edge eng (Maya Chen) 2026-03-13: Found the proxy change that suppresses writes on retransmits. Will prepare a rollback/patch and run canary with LinguaChat's dedicated pool traffic if approved.
Customer (LinguaChat ops contact) 2026-03-13: Confirmed they'll schedule a maintenance window for a canary if we can guarantee minimal disruption. Provided their test device pool for validation.
mitigation_and_workarounds: 1) Short-term: Edge team to roll back proxy v2.17 write-coalescing change to previous behavior (v2.16) for affected dedicated pools (target: 1-hour hotfix).

2) Customer workaround: Reduce client-side keepalive interval to 10s to reduce perceived stall window and enable client reconnect logic that can resume stream using conversation_id (app-level workaround).
3) Fallback: Configure model fallback to small-batched non-streaming endpoint with fail-fast if the HTTP/WS layer reports network retransmit counts above threshold.
resolution: In progress: Edge proxy team preparing hotfix roll-back (v2.16) to remove aggressive write suppression on TCP retransmit events. Plan: roll back to v2.16 for LinguaChat's dedicated pool during low-traffic window, validate with customer test devices, monitor tail latency for 24h. Post-mortem and follow-up PR will add better heuristics for streaming sockets under mobile network conditions.
next_steps: 1) Edge team to schedule rollback in canary (by 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC) and run targeted tests with customer test devices.
2) SRE to instrument additional websocket metrics: retransmit_count, write_suspend_events, per-socket buffer_queued_bytes.
3) Product to assess long-term mitigations: streaming retry semantics, resumable token ranges, and client SDK helpers for mobile reconnection.
4) After stabilization, run a postmortem and notify customer with timeline and permanent fix plan.
